Docs

Docs

Use toil, a structured-JSON CLI and MCP server, to read from and (when allowed) write to databases and the enterprise tools an organization runs, such as issue trackers, source hosts, wikis, CI, artifact repositories, scanners and observability. Use when a task needs data from one of those tools or a database, or mentions `toil` commands, `toil mcp`, a toil connection, or a TOIL_* environment variable.

Docs

toil is the token-efficient alternative to MCP: the same commands as a CLI, each returning one compact envelope, with this skill read a file at a time rather than every tool schema up front. Keep it lean: --select the fields you need, and toil wait rather than polling.

If toil version doesn’t print an envelope, toil isn’t installed yet: install.md, beside this file, says how.

Every call

  • Output. Every command prints one JSON envelope on stdout: { ok, data, error, meta }. Check ok; on failure, error.code says what kind of failure it was and error.fix what to do about it. meta.warnings lists what’s worth knowing that isn’t a failure, and meta.page.nextCursor the next page, when there is one.
  • Two front doors, one command. toil <area> <command> on the command line, or the MCP tool named after its path (db_query) from toil mcp --areas <area>, with identical inputs and output.
  • Writes. Reads are always allowed. A command that changes data needs writes: true on the connection, set by a person, and --allow-write on the call (allowWrite: true over MCP). Only make a write the user asked for. Three writes differ, each listed in core.md under Writes.
  • Connections. Environment variables always win over ~/.toil/config.json. --connection <name> picks one when an area has several; toil connections list names them, never a secret. Setting one up is for a person: a bare toil in a terminal opens a menu for them.
  • Files a command reads or writes stay inside the workspace (--workspace <dir>, else the working directory).
  • Less output. --select <expression> keeps only the fields you name, and toil wait --until <expression> -- <read> repeats a read until it’s true, instead of polling yourself.

Where to look

Open only the file the task needs; each sits beside this one.

FileWhen
core.md--select, toil wait, paging and progress, errors, writes and their exceptions, global flags, files, configuration, the raw api passthrough, dossiers, the audit log, calling toil from a program (@imagile-dev/toil/api), certificates and proxies
<area>.mdOne per area, named after it: jira.md for toil jira …. Its frontmatter says what the area covers; the file gives the oldest version it supports, its credential, its configuration keys and every command
db.mdDatabases: toil db … on every engine
util.mdLocal utilities with no connection or network: toil util …
skills.mdSkills marketplaces, and keeping this skill installed
mcp.mdRunning toil as an MCP server and registering it with an agent
install.mdInstalling toil, and this skill

toil --help lists the areas this install has.

Every page

  • Using toil

    What every toil command shares, in detail - the envelope and errors, the contract version, --select, toil wait, paging and progress, writes and their exceptions, global flags, files and the workspace, configuration, the raw API passthrough, dossiers, the audit log, using toil from a program (@imagile-dev/toil/api), certificates and proxies

  • Databases

    Schemas, tables, describe, row previews, read-only queries with paging, and gated writes on databases (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle)

  • Installing toil

    Installing toil from npm or from a clone with no npm install, the toil alias for a clone, and installing this skill for Codex, GitHub Copilot or Claude Code

  • toil as an MCP server

    Running toil as an MCP server over stdio, the tools and resources it serves, and registering it with Claude Code, Codex, VS Code and other clients

  • Skills marketplaces

    Agent skills from git-hosted marketplaces, installed into the folders Codex, GitHub Copilot and Claude Code read, and switched on and off

  • Local utilities

    Local utilities with no connection or network, decoding a JWT, inventorying dependencies from manifests and lockfiles, checked encoding and hashing, decoding certificates and checking a chain, summarising test, SARIF and coverage reports, triaging a large log, scanning for secrets before a commit or post, sizing files and folders before reading them, time zone, duration, business-day and cron arithmetic, comparing versions and ranges for npm, NuGet and Maven, converting Markdown to and from Jira and Confluence formats, reading OpenAPI documents, drawing C4 architecture diagrams from a JSON model, and mapping Jira, Azure DevOps and GitHub work items to Open Work Items

  • The welcome menu
  • Toil UI

    Toil UI: a local web app to see and reason about work across Jira, Azure DevOps and GitHub, on toil. Alpha, local only.
